cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Yes, but My Way
cards.instruction: Agree with others, then reinterpret the agreement entirely in your favor.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Yes, I'll look after your dog during the kitchen repairs. Bring him over after his walk.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He needs to stay overnight too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Absolutely. Stay in my guest room; you can handle breakfast while I sleep.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can stay, but his six o'clock walk is your job.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Agreed. I'll organise it: lead by the door, your alarm at five thirty. You won't have to plan a thing.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 decides and A3 postpones questions, but A3 agreement and A5 organization would work unchanged without the approval stance.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 overnight need causes A3 guest-room arrangement; B4 insists on A walking duty, causing A5 planning-only reinterpretation despite stock preface.

relationship.evidence: B2 explains care duration and B4 accepts lodging but protects the walk agreement, actively negotiating real labor.

heightening.evidence: B4 explicit duty becomes A5 another yes that shifts the physical walk back to B through alarm setting.

specificity.evidence: A1 kitchen repairs and dog care, B2 overnight stay and B4 early walk give coherent domestic responsibilities.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 no-planning-needed offer is earned by B4 duty claim, but A3 stock question restriction disrupts the affirmative pattern.
